questions.explanation: The relevant evidence is the thesis itself, stated carefully. Moral relativism holds that moral truth is relative to a culture or individual. This is the position defended by Protagoras. The claim that moral relativism holds that one morality is objectively correct is a common mistake about the view, often described as "absolutist misreading of relativism". A fair assessment also has to reckon with this worry: it undercuts cross-cultural criticism. A careful reader separates the actual doctrine from the frequent misreading.
questions.hint: Ask what critics of moral relativism most often find problematic.
